course.title: Modern Frontend Web Development with Vue.js — Initial cohort draft
course.shortDescription: Six guided classes covering web foundations and javascript collections; templates and the composition api; props, events and component ownership; forms and validation; apis, routing and shared state; testing and production diagnosis.
course.description:
A guided course for learners who want to build and explain a working student-management application.

Outcomes

  1. Create a responsive academy page with three cards. Extend its dataset to five courses and add category filtering. Explain shallow copying and demonstrate an empty filter result.
  2. Build a reusable CourseCard list and a reactive counter. Add a computed even/odd label and a watcher that records changes. Explain why the label belongs in computed rather than another writable ref.
  3. Build a CourseCard that emits its course ID and a parent showing the selected course. Add a slot for a badge. Reorder the list and verify the correct course remains selected.
  4. Build a registration form with name, email, phone and course. Demonstrate invalid input, a server rejection and a successful retry. Include keyboard-only test notes and explain why frontend validation is insufficient.
  5. Create course list and detail routes plus a dashboard. Add shared account state and simulated API failures. Explain what happens on a direct detail URL and why the API still checks access.
  6. Produce a local production preview and a troubleshooting checklist for a missing asset, failed API request and direct-route 404. Include one interaction test and measured before/after bundle evidence.
course.duration: 6 classes · 18 live hours plus independent practice
course.requirements: Basic computer use, a code editor, a browser and a local development environment. Frontend framework tracks assume basic JavaScript; backend tracks include introductory language review.
course.targetAudience: Learners building their first structured web application; instructors should review prerequisites with the cohort.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Represent each course with a stable identifier and meaningful fields. Filter selects a subset while map transforms results. Spread creates a shallow copy: nested objects remain shared unless copied separately. Destructuring extracts named values. Use async functions for readable promise-based workflows, with a visible error path for rejected operations. The browser consumes API responses and must not contain a database password or private service key.

questions.text: What is the primary responsibility of a frontend application?

options.text: Providing the user interface and interacting with users

questions.explanation: The frontend is responsible for what users see and interact with in a web application. It communicates with backend services when it needs data or server-side operations.

questions.text: Which three technologies form the basic foundation of the web?
questions.explanation: HTML provides the structure, CSS controls presentation and styling, and JavaScript provides behavior and interactivity.

questions.text: What is Vue.js?

options.text: A JavaScript framework for building user interfaces

questions.explanation: Vue.js is a JavaScript framework designed for building user interfaces. It provides features such as components, reactivity, routing integration, and state-management support.

questions.text: What is a Single-Page Application (SPA)?

options.text: A website containing only one HTML element
An application that generally updates content without full page reloads
A website with only one route

questions.explanation: A SPA typically loads the application shell once and then updates parts of the page as users navigate or interact with the application.

questions.text: What is an API commonly used for in a frontend application?
questions.explanation: An API provides a way for the frontend to communicate with the backend. For example, a Vue application can request a list of courses from a Django or Laravel API.

questions.text: Which is a common architecture for a Vue frontend connected to a backend?
questions.explanation: The frontend normally communicates with the backend through an API. The backend handles business logic and communicates with the database. This also prevents the frontend from directly exposing database credentials.

questions.text: Which keyword declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: `const` prevents reassignment of the variable. It is commonly preferred when the variable itself does not need to be reassigned.

questions.text: Which method creates a new array by transforming each item?
questions.explanation: `map()` runs a function on every item and returns a new array containing the transformed results.

questions.text: Which method returns items that satisfy a condition?
questions.explanation: `filter()` creates a new array containing only the elements for which the supplied condition returns true.

questions.text: What does destructuring allow you to do?

options.text: Extract values from arrays or objects

questions.explanation: Destructuring provides a convenient way to extract values from objects or arrays into variables.

class.objectives: Explain templates and the composition api; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: Vue connects reactive state to a template. A component groups that template with its behavior, allowing one course card design to serve many records.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Use ref for a reactive value and access its value property in script. Templates unwrap refs in common expressions. Use computed for derived values such as whether a counter is even; use watch when a change must trigger an external action. Use v-if for conditional content and v-for with stable keys for lists. Do not compute a second mutable copy of a value that can be derived from existing state.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

<script setup>
import { ref, computed } from 'vue';
const count = ref(0);
const even = computed(() => count.value % 2 === 0);
</script>
<template><button @click="count++">{{ count }}: {{ even ? 'even' : 'odd' }}</button></template>

questions.text: What is a Vue component?

options.text: A reusable piece of UI and logic

questions.explanation: Components allow an application to be divided into smaller, reusable pieces. For example, an LMS could have `CourseCard`, `StudentProfile`, and `Navbar` components.

questions.text: What file extension is commonly used for Vue Single-File Components?
questions.explanation: Vue Single-File Components normally use the `.vue` extension. A component can contain its template, JavaScript logic, and styling in one file.

questions.text: Which syntax displays a JavaScript value inside a Vue template?
questions.explanation: Vue uses double curly braces for text interpolation. For example, `{{ student.name }}` displays the student's name.

questions.text: Which directive is commonly used for conditional rendering?
questions.explanation: `v-if` conditionally renders an element based on an expression. For example, it can display an admin dashboard only when the user has the appropriate role.

questions.text: Which directive is commonly used to render a list?
questions.explanation: `v-for` is used to iterate over arrays or other collections and generate elements or components for each item.

questions.text: Which directive is commonly used to handle events?
questions.explanation: `v-on` listens for DOM events such as clicks and keyboard events. The shorthand `@click` is commonly used instead of `v-on:click`.

questions.text: What is Vue's reactivity system used for?

options.text: Automatically responding to changes in application state

questions.explanation: Vue's reactivity system tracks changes to reactive data and updates the relevant parts of the user interface when that data changes.

questions.text: Which function is commonly used to create reactive state in the Composition API?
questions.explanation: `ref()` creates a reactive reference. In JavaScript, its value is accessed through `.value`, while Vue templates generally unwrap refs automatically.

questions.text: What property is commonly used to access the value of a `ref` in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: If `count` is created with `ref(0)`, JavaScript code accesses its current value using `count.value`.

questions.text: What is `computed()` primarily useful for?
questions.explanation: A computed property derives a value from other reactive data. For example, a student's total score or course completion percentage can be computed from other state.

class.title: 03. Props, events and component ownership
class.objectives: Explain props, events and component ownership; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A component contract defines what a child receives and what it reports to its parent. Explicit contracts make reusable cards easier to understand and test.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Pass course information through props and emit an enroll event containing the course ID. The parent owns enrollment state and decides what to do with the event. Avoid mutating a prop or a nested object received from the parent. A slot lets a parent supply presentation content without forcing the child to know every layout. Keep emitted event names and payloads consistent, and use stable record IDs instead of array positions when items can move.

const emit = defineEmits(['enroll']);
</script>
<template><button @click="emit('enroll', props.course.id)">Enroll</button></template>

questions.text: What are props used for?

options.text: Passing data from a parent component to a child

questions.explanation: Props allow a parent component to provide data to a child component. For example, a parent can pass course information to a `CourseCard`.

questions.text: How does a child component normally communicate an event to its parent?
questions.explanation: A child component can emit a custom event that the parent listens for. This creates a clear communication pattern between components.

questions.text: What is the purpose of `emit`?

options.text: To send custom events from a component

questions.explanation: Emitting events allows a child component to notify its parent that something happened, such as a user clicking an "Enroll" button.

questions.text: What is a slot used for?
questions.explanation: Slots allow a component to accept custom content from its parent. This makes components more flexible and reusable.

questions.text: What is `v-model` commonly used for?

options.text: Two-way binding of form input data

questions.explanation: `v-model` simplifies keeping form input values synchronized with component state. It is commonly used with text inputs, selects, checkboxes, and other form controls.

questions.text: Why are reusable components useful?

options.text: They reduce duplicated UI and logic
They remove the need for APIs

questions.explanation: Reusable components make applications easier to maintain. A single `Button` or `CourseCard` component can be reused throughout an application instead of recreating the same code repeatedly.

questions.text: A child CourseCard needs to request enrollment. What should it send?

options.text: An emitted event containing the course ID
A mutation of the parent prop
An array index as permanent identity

questions.explanation: The parent owns the action and can use the stable course ID.

questions.text: What is a slot useful for in a reusable card?
questions.explanation: Slots allow composition without teaching the child every possible layout.

questions.text: A list can be reordered. Which key should identify each course?

options.text: A new random number on each render

questions.explanation: Stable identity preserves the relationship between a record and its rendered component.

questions.text: A child wants to change a prop received from a parent. What is the preferred contract?

options.text: Write to the URL password field
Emit an event and let the parent update its state
Copy the entire application into the child

questions.explanation: Explicit events keep ownership of parent state clear.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A form is a conversation with the user: labels explain what is needed, validation explains what to fix, and submission state explains what is happening.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Use v-model to bind form state and handle submit at the form level so Enter works. Apply appropriate input types and visible labels. Validate required fields and display field errors near the associated inputs. Backend validation remains authoritative. Keep entered values after a failed request and disable repeated submission only while pending. Custom controls must preserve keyboard interaction and an accessible name.

questions.text: Which Vue directive is commonly used with form inputs?
questions.explanation: `v-model` provides a convenient way to synchronize form input values with reactive state.

questions.text: Why is client-side validation useful?

options.text: It provides immediate feedback to users

questions.explanation: Client-side validation improves the user experience by identifying common input problems immediately. However, it should not be considered a replacement for backend validation.

questions.text: Should backend validation still be performed when frontend validation exists?
questions.explanation: Frontend validation can be bypassed because users control the client application. The backend must independently validate incoming data before processing it.

questions.text: What should an application display while a long form submission is being processed?
questions.explanation: A loading state tells the user that their request is being processed. It can also prevent them from accidentally submitting the form multiple times.

questions.text: A registration form receives invalid email data from the backend. What should the frontend ideally do?
questions.explanation: Backend validation errors should be communicated clearly to the user so they can correct the submitted information.

questions.text: Why should submit buttons sometimes be disabled while a request is processing?
questions.explanation: If a user clicks a submit button multiple times while the first request is still processing, duplicate records or transactions could potentially be created. Disabling the button helps prevent this.

questions.text: Which Vue directive binds a text field to form state?
questions.explanation: v-model coordinates a field value with reactive state.

questions.text: A server rejects a registration. What should the form preserve?
questions.explanation: Retained values support correction and retry without starting over.

questions.text: How should a form support the Enter key?

options.text: Handle submission on the form element
Only use a pointer-click handler on a div

questions.explanation: Form submission semantics support keyboard interaction.

questions.text: Which validation layer can enforce rules against a direct HTTP client?
questions.explanation: A direct caller can bypass all browser-side checks.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: An application needs shareable screen addresses and a clear policy for where remote data lives. Keep route state, local interaction state and shared account state distinct.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Create loading, error, empty and success branches for API requests. Avoid allowing a slow earlier request to replace a later result. Route parameters identify a detail resource; query parameters can preserve filters. A Pinia store can coordinate shared account information, while temporary field state usually belongs in the form. A route guard controls navigation, but the backend must independently reject unauthorized data requests.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

async function loadCourses() {
  loading.value = true; error.value = '';
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/api/courses');
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Could not load courses');
    courses.value = await response.json();
  } catch (e) { error.value = e.message; }
  finally { loading.value = false; }
}

questions.text: Which HTTP method is normally used to retrieve data?
questions.explanation: GET requests are generally used to retrieve resources from a server, such as retrieving a list of courses.

questions.text: Which format is commonly used for API data?
questions.explanation: JSON is widely used for exchanging structured data between frontend applications and backend APIs because it is lightweight and easy for JavaScript applications to process.

questions.text: Which HTTP method is commonly used to create a new resource?
questions.explanation: POST is commonly used when sending data to a server to create a new resource, such as registering a new student.

questions.text: What should a Vue application usually do while waiting for an API response?
questions.explanation: Displaying a loading state provides feedback to the user and makes it clear that the application is still processing the request.

questions.text: What does HTTP status code 401 generally indicate?
questions.explanation: A 401 response generally indicates that authentication is required or that the provided authentication credentials are not valid.

questions.text: A Vue application needs to display courses from a Django API. What is the appropriate approach?

options.text: Request the course data through the API
Connect Vue directly to the database

questions.explanation: The Vue application should communicate with the Django backend through an API. The backend controls database access and business logic rather than exposing the database directly to the browser.

questions.text: What is Vue Router used for?
questions.explanation: Vue Router allows a Vue application to define different routes and display different components based on the current URL.

questions.text: What is a route parameter?

options.text: A value included in a URL route

questions.explanation: A route parameter represents dynamic information in a URL. For example, `/courses/25` could use `25` as the course ID.

questions.text: What would `/courses/:id` commonly represent?
questions.explanation: `:id` represents a dynamic route parameter. Different course IDs can therefore use the same route structure.

questions.text: What is a navigation guard commonly used for?
questions.explanation: Navigation guards can be used to determine whether a user should be allowed to navigate to a route. For example, an LMS might protect its student dashboard from unauthenticated users.

Explain how a Vue application communicates with a backend API. Describe the purpose of loading, success, and error states.

Connect your Vue application to a public or locally created API. Retrieve and display a list of courses. Add loading and error handling.

class.title: 06. Testing and production diagnosis
class.objectives: Explain testing and production diagnosis; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A production build changes asset paths and configuration, so development success alone does not establish deployment readiness. Use evidence to diagnose a blank page.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Inspect the console for script failures and the network panel for missing assets or rejected API requests. Check the host SPA fallback for direct routes, the configured public API URL and cross-origin response headers. Test visible behavior such as emitted enrollment events and error recovery. Lazy-load routes when it reduces initial work; measure the resulting build. Never embed private credentials in browser environment variables.

questions.text: What is the purpose of automated testing?

options.text: To automatically check that software behaves as expected

questions.explanation: Automated tests allow developers to repeatedly verify that application functionality works correctly and that new changes have not introduced unexpected problems.

questions.text: What is a unit test?

options.text: A test of a small isolated piece of functionality
A test of an entire production server

questions.explanation: A unit test focuses on a small piece of functionality, such as a JavaScript function or a particular piece of application logic.

questions.text: What tool can help developers inspect Vue components during development?
questions.explanation: Vue DevTools provides development tools for inspecting Vue components, application state, events, and other useful information.

questions.text: What is lazy loading useful for?

options.text: Loading resources or features only when needed

questions.explanation: Lazy loading can reduce the amount of JavaScript that needs to be loaded initially. For example, an admin section can be loaded only when an administrator visits it.

questions.text: Which is an important accessibility practice?

options.text: Providing meaningful labels for form controls

questions.explanation: Meaningful labels help users understand form controls and improve accessibility for people using assistive technologies.

questions.text: Why should large Vue applications be organized into reusable components?

options.text: To improve maintainability and reduce duplication

questions.explanation: Breaking a large application into logical reusable components makes the code easier to understand, test, maintain, and modify.

questions.text: Which command commonly creates a production build in a modern Vue project?
questions.explanation: In a typical Vue project created with Vite, `npm run build` creates an optimized production build that can be deployed to a web server or hosting platform.

questions.text: Where is the production build commonly generated in a Vite-powered Vue project?
questions.explanation: Vite normally places the generated production files inside the `dist` directory. These are the files that can be deployed to static hosting.

questions.text: Why are environment variables useful?

options.text: They automatically encrypt all application data
They allow configuration such as API URLs to vary between environments

questions.explanation: Environment-specific configuration allows the application to use different values in development, testing, and production. For example, development might use a local API while production uses a deployed API.

questions.text: Should a secret API key that must remain private normally be placed in frontend JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Frontend JavaScript is delivered to the user's browser, meaning users can inspect it. Truly private secrets should remain on a trusted backend rather than being embedded in client-side code.

**Question 17 — Theory**
Explain why testing, accessibility, performance optimization, and good component organization are important in a production Vue application.

**Question 18 — Practical/Research**
Research two Vue performance techniques, such as lazy loading, component optimization, or efficient rendering. Apply at least one technique to a small Vue application and explain the improvement.

**Question 19 — Hands-on**
Build a production version of your Vue application and deploy it to a hosting platform. Configure the production API URL and test the deployed application.
